Overview: General-purpose conversational assistant built on OpenAI's GPT model family. Handles open-ended dialogue, reasoning, document and image analysis, code generation, web-grounded research and agentic task execution from a single chat surface.
Main Features: Multimodal input (text, image, file, voice); Deep Research; Advanced Voice Mode; Canvas collaborative editor; Custom GPTs and GPT Store; Projects and memory; Codex coding agent; Sora video generation on top tiers; connectors to Drive/SharePoint/GitHub.
Intended Audience: Everyone from casual consumers to knowledge workers, developers, students and enterprise teams.
Use Cases: Drafting and editing documents; summarising long PDFs and reports; brainstorming; translation; data analysis on uploaded spreadsheets; coding help and debugging; customer-facing copy; market and competitive research.
Best For: Broad daily knowledge work where one assistant must cover writing, analysis and code.
Pricing Model: Freemium subscription; per-seat for business; separate token-metered API
Pricing Plans: Free $0 (ad-supported since the 2026 ad rollout). Go $8/mo. Plus $20/mo. Pro sold as two usage tiers: $100/mo (5x Plus usage) and $200/mo (20x Plus usage, priority compute, ~250 Deep Research tasks). Business $20/seat/mo annual or $25/seat/mo monthly (2-seat minimum; cut from $25/$30 in April 2026); a Premium seat runs roughly $100-125. Enterprise custom, annual contract. API billed per token, separate bill.
Billing Period: Monthly for individuals; monthly or annual per seat for Business; annual for Enterprise
Usage Limits: Free and Go have capped uploads, image generation, voice, deep research and memory. Plus uses a rolling message cap resetting every few hours plus a weekly cap on extended-reasoning messages. Pro is 'unlimited subject to abuse guardrails' with no published cap. Context tops out around 128K instant / 400K reasoning tokens on Pro.
Free Plan: Yes - permanent free tier with unlimited everyday text chat, but ad-supported and with separate caps on uploads, images, voice and research.
Free Trial: No standalone free trial of Plus/Pro; the free tier serves that purpose. Business trials are handled through sales.
Platforms: Web, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android; Chrome/Edge extensions; Atlas browser
Languages: 50+ conversational languages including Arabic, French and English; UI localised in a smaller set
API: Yes - OpenAI Platform API, token-metered and billed separately from ChatGPT plans
Integrations: Google Drive, OneDrive/SharePoint, GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Box, Zapier; MCP connectors; custom GPT actions
Advantages: Largest feature surface of any consumer assistant; strongest third-party ecosystem; excellent multimodal handling; agentic Codex and Operator tooling; mature enterprise controls on Business/Enterprise.
Limitations: Pricing tiers are confusing (two plans both badged 'Pro'); free and Go tiers now carry ads; consumer plans train on your data by default unless you opt out; message caps interrupt heavy sessions on Plus; model routing is not shown to the user.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Rollout of new models varies by account, region and plan, so two users on the same tier may see different models. Business/Enterprise exclude training on your data by default; consumer tiers require a settings change.
Evidence / Sources: openai.com/chatgpt/pricing; help.openai.com plan articles; OpenAI Business pricing page
Logo Source: https://openai.com/brand/ - logo files with usage rules
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Brand assets downloadable; logo use permitted under OpenAI Brand Guidelines. Do not alter marks or imply endorsement.

Overview: Conversational assistant from Anthropic focused on long-context reasoning, careful writing, document analysis and agentic coding. Strong on following detailed instructions and handling very large inputs.
Main Features: Very long context windows (200K up to 1M tokens); Artifacts (live documents, code and apps in-chat); Projects with shared knowledge; Research mode; Claude Code CLI and IDE agent; Cowork agentic desktop app; memory; connectors and MCP; file creation (xlsx/docx/pptx/pdf).
Intended Audience: Writers, analysts, researchers, lawyers, developers and enterprise teams handling long or sensitive documents.
Use Cases: Analysing long contracts, RFPs and technical specs; drafting and refining professional writing; multi-file code refactoring; building internal tools via Artifacts; structured data extraction from documents.
Best For: Long-document analysis, careful professional writing, and agentic coding across a whole codebase.
Pricing Model: Freemium subscription; per-seat Team/Enterprise; separate token-metered API
Pricing Plans: Free $0. Pro $20/mo or $200/yr (~$17/mo effective). Max in two tiers: $100/mo (5x Pro) and $200/mo (20x Pro). Team from $25/seat/mo (about $20/seat annual) for standard seats, with a higher premium seat tier. Enterprise custom. Education plans for institutions. API separate: Fable 5.1 $10/$50 per 1M in/out tokens, Opus 5 $5/$25, Sonnet 5 $2/$10, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5.
Billing Period: Monthly or annual (Pro and Team); Enterprise annual contract
Usage Limits: Every subscription meters usage against a rolling 5-hour session window plus a weekly ceiling, shared across chat and Claude Code. Free defaults to Sonnet with a rolling budget rather than a message count. Max raises capacity but is not unlimited.
Free Plan: Yes - free tier includes Sonnet access, web search, memory, Artifacts, file creation, code execution and connectors. Claude Code, Opus, Fable and Research mode need a paid tier.
Free Trial: No separate trial; the free tier is the trial. Enterprise trials through sales.
Platforms: Web, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android; Claude Code (terminal, VS Code, JetBrains); Chrome extension; Excel/PowerPoint add-ins; Slack
Languages: Strong multilingual coverage incl. Arabic, French, English; UI in several languages
API: Yes - Claude Platform / Anthropic API, plus availability on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry
Integrations: Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, GitHub, Slack, Jira, Confluence, Asana, Notion, Canva, Figma, Stripe; MCP servers; Zapier
Advantages: Best-in-class long context; very strong instruction following and writing quality; Artifacts and file creation produce usable deliverables, not just text; Team/Enterprise exclude training at contract level; MCP gives a clean integration story.
Limitations: Session and weekly caps can bite hard during agentic coding; image generation is not native; smaller plugin ecosystem than ChatGPT; Anthropic's own pages have at times been inconsistent about annual Max pricing.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Max is a capacity tier, not a feature tier - it unlocks no models Pro lacks. Claude Code consumes the same pool as chat, so heavy terminal use exhausts a Pro plan quickly.
Evidence / Sources: claude.com/pricing; Anthropic Help Center plan articles; anthropic.com/pricing for API rates
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Brand kit provides logos and wordmarks with published usage rules. Screenshots of the product are generally acceptable for editorial/review use.

Overview: Google's multimodal assistant, sold through the Google AI consumer subscription ladder (formerly 'Gemini Advanced') and bundled into Google Workspace. Combines chat, search grounding, image and video generation, and deep Workspace integration.
Main Features: Gemini 3.x model family with 1M-token context; Deep Research; Veo video generation and Flow editor; Deep Think reasoning on top tiers; Gemini Spark background agent; Antigravity agentic dev platform; Jules coding agent; NotebookLM; Canvas; Google Workspace side panels.
Intended Audience: Google Workspace and Android users, students, creators, developers and enterprises already on Google Cloud.
Use Cases: Drafting in Docs and Gmail; analysing Sheets; summarising Drive files; research with live search grounding; video and image generation for marketing; Android on-device assistance.
Best For: Anyone already inside Google Workspace/Drive who wants AI where their files already live.
Pricing Model: Freemium consumer subscription bundled with Google One storage; Workspace seat licensing; token-metered API
Pricing Plans: Free $0. Google AI Plus $4.99/mo (cut from $7.99 on 8 June 2026; 400 GB storage, 2x free limits). Google AI Pro $19.99/mo (4x limits, 5 TB storage, YouTube Premium Lite, Google Home Premium, 1,000 Flow credits). Google AI Ultra in two tiers since I/O 2026: $99.99/mo (5x Pro, 20 TB) and $199.99/mo (20x Pro, reduced from $249.99; adds Project Genie). Annual billing now available on every paid plan. Gemini is bundled into Workspace Business Standard/Plus/Enterprise - the standalone Workspace add-on was dropped in 2025.
Usage Limits: Compute-based rather than message-count limits: a heavy Deep Research session burns quota far faster than plain chat, so identical plans can hit walls at different times. Extra AI credits are sold when quota runs out. Newest Flash models are restricted to Pro/Ultra in the app; free tier stays on an older Flash.
Free Plan: Yes - free Gemini app access with capped limits and older model routing.
Free Trial: No continuously available trial; promotional trials appear periodically (e.g. device and carrier bundles). Google AI Studio is free with daily request limits and no card.
Platforms: Web, Android (deep OS integration), iOS, Chrome, Workspace apps (Docs, Sheets, Gmail, Slides, Meet)
Languages: 40+ languages including Arabic, French and English
API: Yes - Gemini API via Google AI Studio and Vertex AI. Gemini 3.1 Pro ~$2/$12 per 1M tokens (200K context), $4/$18 above; Flash tiers around $0.75/$3.75 on introductory pricing to 31 Dec 2026.
Integrations: Google Workspace end-to-end, Google Cloud/Vertex, Android, Chrome, YouTube, Google Home; third-party via API
Advantages: Unmatched bundle value - 5 TB storage plus YouTube Premium Lite at the $19.99 tier; native Workspace integration; 1M-token context standard; strongest consumer video generation via Veo.
Limitations: Plan names 'AI Plus' vs 'AI Pro' are easy to confuse; compute-based quotas are opaque; some Ultra features are US-only (Gemini Spark) or locked to the $199.99 tier (Project Genie); pricing restructured twice in 2026.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Anyone already paying for Google One storage should net that saving off the $19.99 before comparing to ChatGPT or Claude. Ultra's 'starting at $99.99' hides a real feature split between the two Ultra tiers.
Evidence / Sources: one.google.com/about/google-ai-plans; blog.google Google I/O 2026 subscription update; ai.google.dev pricing
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Logos and product screenshots governed by Google Brand Permissions; editorial/review use generally permitted, commercial use needs approval.

Overview: AI assistant embedded across Microsoft 365 - Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams and Windows - grounded in your organisation's own tenant data via Microsoft Graph. Also available as a free consumer chat assistant.
Main Features: Copilot in Word (draft/rewrite/summarise), Excel (formulas, analysis, charts), PowerPoint (deck generation), Outlook (triage and drafting), Teams (meeting recap and action items); Copilot Chat (web-grounded, no extra cost); Copilot Studio for custom agents; Agent 365; Copilot Credits for metered agent work.
Intended Audience: Organisations already standardised on Microsoft 365; enterprise IT, finance, HR, sales and operations teams.
Use Cases: Meeting recaps and action items from Teams; inbox triage in Outlook; first-draft documents grounded in SharePoint content; Excel analysis; deck generation from a Word doc; custom agents over internal data.
Best For: Organisations whose day already runs through Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel.
Pricing Model: Per-user add-on licence on top of a qualifying Microsoft 365 base plan; plus consumption-based Copilot Credits
Pricing Plans: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Enterprise) $30/user/mo, annual commitment - requires a qualifying base licence (E3, E5, Business Standard/Premium, E1, F1/F3). Microsoft 365 Copilot Business $21/user/mo annual ($25.20 monthly) for orgs up to 300 users; a promotional $18/user/mo runs 1 July - 31 December 2026 (annual commitment, first year only, not on trials). Bundles introduced 1 July 2026: Business Standard + Copilot $23.50/user/mo; Business Premium + Copilot $32/user/mo; E7 Frontier Suite $99/user/mo. Copilot Studio from $200/mo per tenant. Copilot Credits $0.01 each pay-as-you-go, or $200 for 25,000 credits/mo prepaid.
Billing Period: Annual commitment for the headline rates; monthly option at a premium
Usage Limits: Copilot cannot be bought standalone - a qualifying M365 licence is mandatory. Business SKU capped at 300 users and Microsoft can enforce that limit. Agent actions consume Copilot Credits, so complex multi-step tasks cost more than simple ones. Pay-as-you-go credits require an Azure subscription.
Free Plan: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is included at no extra per-user cost for many M365 users (web-grounded chat only, not in-app Copilot). A free consumer Copilot app also exists.
Free Trial: Trials available through Microsoft and partners; promotional pricing explicitly excluded from trial subscriptions.
Platforms: Windows, web, iOS, Android, Microsoft 365 desktop and web apps, Teams, Edge
Languages: Broad Microsoft 365 language coverage incl. Arabic, French, English
API: Indirect - Copilot Studio, Microsoft Graph API, Azure AI Foundry
Integrations: Entire Microsoft 365 / Graph estate, SharePoint, OneDrive, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, Teams; third-party connectors via Copilot Studio
Advantages: Tenant-grounded answers using your real documents and email; unmatched depth inside Office apps; enterprise-grade compliance, data residency and admin controls; no data leaves the Microsoft compliance boundary.
Limitations: The $30 headline is never the total - add the base suite and the real all-in figure is roughly $66-90/user/mo on E3/E5. Every assigned seat costs the same whether used or not; Microsoft reports ~15M paid seats against 450M+ commercial users (~3.3% penetration). Gartner's 2026 assessment says value realisation is not guaranteed.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: In most small offices only two to four people per ten get real value - typically those whose day is the inbox, the Teams meeting and long Word/Excel files. Licensing the rest is how a $756 decision becomes a $2,520 one.
Evidence / Sources: microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot pricing pages; Microsoft licensing FAQ; Microsoft 1 July 2026 SKU announcement
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Microsoft Trademark & Brand Guidelines govern use. Screenshots permitted under Microsoft's general screenshot policy for accurate, non-disparaging depiction.

Overview: Conversational assistant from xAI with a deliberately less filtered personality and live grounding in the X (Twitter) firehose. Positioned as a real-time-aware chatbot with image generation and voice.
Main Features: Real-time X/web data access; DeepSearch and DeeperSearch research modes; Think mode for step-by-step reasoning; Aurora/Grok Imagine image and video generation; voice mode; Companions; multiple personality modes.
Intended Audience: X users, consumers who want real-time social-media awareness, developers, and users who dislike heavy content filtering.
Use Cases: Tracking breaking news and social sentiment in real time; informal research; image generation; casual conversation; coding help; summarising X threads.
Best For: Real-time awareness of what is being said on X right now.
Pricing Model: Freemium; bundled with X Premium tiers; separate API
Pricing Plans: Free tier with rate limits. SuperGrok around $30/mo. SuperGrok Heavy around $300/mo for the highest limits and earliest model access. Also bundled into X Premium+ (price varies by region and has changed repeatedly). xAI API billed per token, separate.
Usage Limits: Free tier has tight query and image-generation caps that reset on a rolling window. DeepSearch and Think modes have separate, lower caps.
Free Plan: Yes - free tier with meaningful rate limits, accessible on grok.com and in the X app.
Free Trial: Occasional promotional free periods; no standing trial.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, integrated in the X app
Languages: Multilingual, strongest in English; Arabic and French supported but less polished
API: Yes - xAI API, token-metered, OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Integrations: X platform native; Tesla vehicles; Azure AI Foundry; third-party via API
Advantages: Genuinely real-time social data no competitor matches; fast; permissive content policy suits some creative and research work; image generation included at low tiers.
Limitations: Pricing and plan names have changed frequently and are poorly documented; less filtered output is a compliance risk in corporate settings; enterprise governance features are immature; accuracy on X-sourced claims depends on the quality of the underlying posts.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Verify current tier names and prices directly - Grok's plan structure has been among the least stable in the market. Not recommended as a system of record for regulated industries.
Evidence / Sources: grok.com; x.ai/api; X Premium help pages
Screenshot / Reuse Information: No published open brand kit; contact xAI before commercial reuse of marks.

Overview: AI answer engine that runs a live web search for every question and returns a synthesised answer with inline citations. Lets you choose which frontier model answers, and bundles an agentic browser.
Main Features: Cited answers with source list; Pro Search multi-step retrieval; Spaces (file-grounded workspaces); Labs for generating reports, dashboards and small apps; Comet agentic browser (free since Oct 2025); Perplexity Computer orchestrating 19 model sub-agents; Model Council running a query across three frontier models and synthesising.
Intended Audience: Researchers, analysts, journalists, students, consultants and anyone who needs sourced answers rather than prose.
Use Cases: Competitive and market research; fact-checking with traceable sources; literature scanning; due diligence; travel and purchase research; replacing a Google-plus-reading workflow.
Best For: Any question where you need the answer AND the sources it came from.
Pricing Model: Freemium subscription; per-seat enterprise; separate Sonar API
Pricing Plans: Free $0. Pro $20/mo or $200/yr (~$16.67/mo, ~17% saving). Max $200/mo or ~$2,000/yr (~$167/mo; annual sold on web only, not App Store/Play). Education Pro $10/mo for verified students and educators via SheerID. Enterprise Pro $40/seat/mo or $400/yr. Enterprise Max $325/seat/mo. Comet Plus add-on $5. Sonar API from $1 per 1M tokens up to $15 per 1M output on Sonar Pro, plus per-request search fees.
Billing Period: Monthly or annual; enterprise seats annual
Usage Limits: Free tier gives unlimited basic searches but roughly 5 Pro Searches per day and no frontier models. Pro includes Spaces up to 50 files and $40 of Perplexity Computer credits. Max removes the Labs quota and raises file storage to ~5,000 files per Space. A credit system was introduced in 2026 and limits were quietly tightened.
Free Plan: Yes - permanent free plan with cited answers across web, iOS, Android, Mac and Windows.
Free Trial: No standing trial, but heavy promotional activity: Comet download has granted a free Pro month; carrier bundles (Airtel India, Xfinity US, Bell Canada) have given 12 months free. Many circulating offers are expired or region-locked.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Comet browser, Chrome extension
Languages: Multilingual answers incl. Arabic, French, English; sources retrieved in the query language
API: Yes - Sonar API, per-token plus per-request search billing
Integrations: Comet browser, Chrome extension, Raycast, Zapier, Slack (enterprise); file upload from Drive/Dropbox in Spaces
Advantages: Best-in-class citation discipline; one $20 fee buys access to GPT, Claude and Gemini models; genuinely fast; Comet is a capable free agentic browser; student pricing is half price permanently.
Limitations: It is an answer engine, not a workflow engine - it will not act in your inbox or CRM. The official pricing page sits behind a bot wall, so third-party guides disagree on fine print. Plan lineup was trimmed from six SKUs to four core surfaces on 5 July 2026. Enterprise Max at $325/seat is expensive relative to alternatives.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: For normal use the free tier or $20 Pro is the relevant price; Max is priced for heavy agent and automation use, not ordinary search. Verify any plan not currently listed before budgeting.
Evidence / Sources: perplexity.ai/pricing; Perplexity release notes (Feb and Mar 2026); docs.perplexity.ai for Sonar rates
Logo Source: https://www.perplexity.ai/ - brand assets in footer/press kit
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Press kit available; editorial use of screenshots generally permitted with attribution.

Overview: Small independent, privacy-first AI search engine that answers conversationally and strips ads, trackers and clutter from results. Positions itself as a calm, safe alternative to mainstream search.
Main Features: Conversational answers with sources; ad-free and tracker-free by design; no user profiling or search history retention; reader mode that extracts clean article text; summarise-any-page function; visual search results; kid-safe filtering.
Intended Audience: Privacy-conscious individuals, students, educators, parents and users on low-bandwidth connections.
Use Cases: Everyday search without ad tracking; reading long articles distraction-free; safe search for classrooms and families; quick summarisation of a URL.
Best For: Private, ad-free everyday search with clean reading.
Pricing Model: Free product; no published paid tier
Pricing Plans: Free. No paid subscription published as of the check date. The team has historically funded development through grants and small-scale support rather than subscriptions.
Usage Limits: No published hard limits; fair-use rate limiting applies. Capability is well below frontier assistants.
Free Plan: Yes - the entire product is free.
Free Trial: n/a
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, Chrome extension
Languages: Primarily English; other languages handled but less reliably
API: No public API published
Integrations: Browser extension; set as default search engine
Advantages: Genuinely no ads and no tracking; very fast and lightweight; clean reader mode is excellent; safe for classroom use; free with no account required.
Limitations: Much weaker reasoning and synthesis than Perplexity or ChatGPT; small index and limited freshness; no API; tiny team means uncertain long-term viability; little non-English depth.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Best treated as a privacy-respecting search front end rather than a research assistant. Confirm the project is still actively maintained before standardising on it.
Evidence / Sources: andisearch.com; Andi blog and about page
Logo Source: Logo on site; no formal press kit published
Screenshot / Reuse Information: No published reuse policy - request permission before commercial reuse.

Overview: Agentic search product that generates custom 'Sparkpages' - purpose-built summary pages assembled for your query - and runs multi-step agents including an AI phone caller, slide generator and deep research agent.
Main Features: Sparkpages (AI-generated, ad-free result pages); Super Agent for multi-step autonomous tasks; AI Slides and AI Sheets; AI Designer; AI Phone Call agent that actually dials businesses; Deep Research; cross-check agent for factual verification.
Intended Audience: Researchers, small-business owners, marketers and anyone who wants a search engine that also executes tasks.
Use Cases: Product comparison research on a single generated page; booking or enquiring by AI phone call; generating decks from a research prompt; competitive analysis; travel planning.
Best For: Research questions where you want an assembled page plus an agent that can act on the result.
Pricing Model: Freemium with credit-based agent usage
Pricing Plans: Free tier with daily credits. Plus around $24.99/mo. Pro around $249.99/mo for high-volume agent use. Credits are consumed per agent action, with heavier agents (phone calls, deep research, video) costing far more than a simple search. Verify current tiers - Genspark has repriced repeatedly.
Usage Limits: Credit-metered: agent runs, phone calls and slide generation each draw different credit amounts. Free daily credits exhaust quickly on agent tasks.
Free Plan: Yes - free daily credit allowance covering basic search and light agent use.
Free Trial: Paid features sampled via free credits rather than a time-boxed trial.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android
Languages: Multilingual incl. Chinese, English, Japanese; Arabic and French supported
API: Limited/emerging - check current developer docs
Integrations: Google Drive, Notion, Slack and others via agent connectors; browser extension
Advantages: The AI phone-call agent is a genuinely differentiated capability; Sparkpages are far more readable than a list of blue links; strong all-in-one agent suite for the price of the Plus tier.
Limitations: Credit accounting is opaque and burns fast; quality is inconsistent across agents; young company with rapidly shifting pricing; enterprise governance and data-residency story is thin; phone agent availability is region-limited.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Budget by expected agent runs, not by seats - the credit model is where cost escapes. Treat the Pro tier as an agent-volume purchase.
Evidence / Sources: genspark.ai/pricing; Genspark product blog
Screenshot / Reuse Information: No published reuse terms - request permission.

Overview: Multilingual AI search engine built around cross-language retrieval - it searches in several languages simultaneously and returns a unified, cited answer, then can turn that answer into a mind map or presentation.
Main Features: Cross-language simultaneous search; cited answers; automatic mind-map generation from any answer; one-click presentation generation; Topic Collections; Agent mode for deeper research; real-time translation of sources.
Intended Audience: Multilingual researchers, students, international business teams and anyone working across language barriers - particularly strong for Japanese, Chinese and English.
Use Cases: Researching a topic across sources in languages you do not read; building a visual mind map of a subject; generating a first-draft deck from research; cross-border market research.
Best For: Research that spans languages - especially Asian-language sources.
Pricing Model: Freemium subscription
Pricing Plans: Free tier with daily limits on Pro Search. Pro around $14.99/mo (roughly $8.33/mo billed annually). Higher tiers and team plans exist. Verify - Felo prices have moved and vary by region.
Usage Limits: Free tier caps Pro Search queries per day; mind-map and presentation generation also metered on free.
Free Plan: Yes - free tier with basic search and limited Pro Search per day.
Free Trial: Short Pro trials have been offered promotionally.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android, Chrome extension
Languages: Exceptional multilingual coverage - Japanese, Chinese, Korean, English, French, Arabic and more; cross-language retrieval is the core feature
API: Limited - check current developer documentation
Integrations: Browser extension; export to Notion, PDF, PowerPoint
Advantages: Best cross-language search in the category; automatic mind maps are genuinely useful for structuring a topic; cheaper than Perplexity Pro; presentation export saves real time.
Limitations: Smaller and less known than Perplexity; English-only research shows less advantage; enterprise features and compliance documentation are limited; pricing varies by region and is not always clearly documented.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: The strongest reason to choose Felo over Perplexity is genuinely multilingual source material. For English-only work the advantage largely disappears.
Evidence / Sources: felo.ai/pricing; Felo product documentation
Screenshot / Reuse Information: No published reuse policy - request permission before commercial use.

Overview: AI assistant built into Kagi, a paid ad-free search engine. Grounds answers in Kagi's own high-quality search index and lets you switch between frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and Mistral within one subscription.
Main Features: Model switching across many frontier models; grounding in Kagi's curated search index; custom assistants with system prompts; Lenses for scoping searches; site ranking and blocking to personalise results; Summarizer; no ads and no tracking of any kind.
Intended Audience: Privacy-focused professionals, developers and power searchers willing to pay for search quality and independence.
Use Cases: High-signal technical research; searching without SEO spam; comparing model outputs on the same grounded query; personalising a search index by demoting low-quality domains.
Best For: Professionals who want ad-free, user-controlled search with an assistant attached.
Pricing Model: Paid subscription only (search is the product); Assistant included in paid tiers
Pricing Plans: Starter around $5/mo (300 searches). Professional around $10/mo (unlimited searches, includes Assistant). Ultimate around $25/mo (unlimited searches plus full Assistant access to all frontier models). Team plans priced per seat. Kagi also sells the Orion browser separately. Verify current tiers.
Usage Limits: Starter is capped at a set number of searches per month. Assistant access to the most expensive frontier models is tier-dependent - Ultimate unlocks the full set.
Free Plan: No true free plan - a limited trial of ~100 free searches is offered before payment is required.
Free Trial: Yes - roughly 100 free searches, no card required, to evaluate quality.
Platforms: Web, Orion browser (macOS/iOS), any browser via custom search engine setting
Languages: Multilingual; interface primarily English
API: Yes - Kagi Search API and Summarizer API, usage-priced
Integrations: Browser search-engine integration, Orion browser, API for developers
Advantages: Search result quality is widely regarded as the best available; no ads, no tracking, no user profiling as a business model; one subscription covers many frontier models; site-level ranking control is unique.
Limitations: Paying for search is a hard sell for most users; no free tier; small index relative to Google for very long-tail or local queries; Assistant is good but not differentiated beyond the grounding; limited non-English depth.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: The value case rests on search quality and the absence of an ad model, not on the assistant itself. Worth trialling the 100 free searches on your real queries before committing.
Evidence / Sources: kagi.com/pricing; help.kagi.com documentation
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Kagi publishes documentation openly; confirm mark usage before commercial reuse.

Overview: AI research assistant for systematic literature review. Searches a corpus of ~125 million academic papers, extracts structured data from each into a comparison table, and summarises findings across studies.
Main Features: Semantic paper search across ~125M papers; automatic data extraction into custom table columns; systematic review workflow; screening with custom inclusion criteria; Elicit Reports; PDF upload and extraction; citation export; notebook for multi-step research.
Intended Audience: Academic researchers, PhD students, systematic reviewers, evidence-synthesis teams, pharma and biotech research, policy analysts.
Use Cases: Running a systematic literature review; screening hundreds of abstracts against inclusion criteria; extracting sample sizes, methods and outcomes into a structured table; finding papers on a concept rather than a keyword.
Best For: Systematic reviews and structured evidence extraction at scale.
Pricing Model: Freemium with credit-based extraction; per-seat team and enterprise plans
Pricing Plans: Basic free with a monthly credit allowance. Plus around $12/mo billed annually (about $15 monthly) with a larger credit pool and unlimited search. Pro around $49/mo annually for high-volume extraction and reports. Team and Enterprise priced per seat on request. Credits are consumed per paper column extracted.
Usage Limits: Credit-metered: each cell of extracted data from each paper consumes credits, so a 200-paper, 8-column extraction is expensive. Free tier credits are quickly exhausted by any real review.
Free Plan: Yes - Basic free plan with unlimited search and a limited monthly credit allowance for extraction.
Free Trial: Free plan serves as the trial; institutional pilots arranged through sales.
Platforms: Web (browser only)
Languages: Interface English; indexed literature is predominantly English
API: Enterprise API available on request
Integrations: Zotero, BibTeX/RIS citation export, CSV export, PDF upload
Advantages: Purpose-built for systematic review rather than generic chat; extraction into structured tables is a real time-saver; grounded strictly in the paper corpus so hallucination risk is lower; transparent about which paper each claim came from.
Limitations: Corpus skews heavily toward English-language and open-access literature; paywalled full texts often unavailable so extraction works from abstracts; credit pricing makes large reviews costly; extraction accuracy still requires human verification for publication-grade work.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Always spot-check extracted values against the source PDF - accuracy is good but not publication-grade unverified. Budget credits against the number of papers multiplied by the number of columns, not by seats.
Evidence / Sources: elicit.com/pricing; elicit.com/faq; Elicit documentation
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Academic/editorial use generally acceptable; confirm before commercial reuse.

Overview: Academic search engine that answers yes/no research questions by aggregating findings across peer-reviewed papers and showing a 'Consensus Meter' indicating how much the literature agrees.
Main Features: Consensus Meter showing agreement/disagreement across studies; study snapshots with sample size, methodology and journal quality; Pro Analysis; Copilot for synthesised answers; GPT-4-class summarisation of findings; Semantic Scholar corpus of 200M+ papers; filters by study design and rigour.
Intended Audience: Clinicians, evidence-based practitioners, health and nutrition researchers, science journalists, students.
Use Cases: Answering 'does X cause Y' style questions with literature backing; checking whether a popular health claim is supported; quickly gauging scientific consensus before a deeper review; sourcing citations for a claim.
Best For: Fast evidence checks on empirical yes/no questions.
Pricing Model: Freemium subscription; institutional licensing
Pricing Plans: Free tier with unlimited searches but limited AI credits per month. Premium around $8.99/mo billed annually (about $11.99 monthly) for unlimited GPT-4 summaries, Consensus Meter and Copilot. Enterprise/institutional pricing on request. Student discounts available.
Usage Limits: Free tier limits AI-generated summaries and Consensus Meter uses per month; unlimited plain search remains.
Free Plan: Yes - free plan with unlimited search and a capped number of AI credits monthly.
Free Trial: Free tier acts as the trial; institutional trials via sales.
Platforms: Web; ChatGPT plugin/GPT
Languages: English interface and predominantly English corpus
API: Limited - contact for enterprise access
Integrations: ChatGPT (custom GPT), citation export, Semantic Scholar corpus
Advantages: The Consensus Meter is an unusually honest interface - it shows disagreement rather than manufacturing a confident answer; very cheap; excellent for clinical and nutrition questions; strong study-quality signals.
Limitations: Works best on empirical yes/no questions and poorly on open-ended or theoretical topics; corpus is English-dominant; does not do structured extraction like Elicit; the meter can oversimplify a nuanced literature.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Treat the Consensus Meter as a starting signal, not a verdict - always read the underlying studies for anything consequential. Complements rather than replaces Elicit.
Evidence / Sources: consensus.app/home/pricing; Consensus help centre
Logo Source: Logo and press assets on site
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Editorial use generally acceptable; confirm for commercial reuse.

Overview: Citation analysis platform built around Smart Citations - it shows not just that a paper was cited but whether the citing paper supported, contrasted or merely mentioned the finding, with the surrounding sentence as evidence.
Main Features: Smart Citations classified as supporting / contrasting / mentioning; citation statements with context; Reference Check for manuscripts (flags retracted or heavily contrasted references); Scite Assistant chat over the citation graph; dashboards for institutions; browser extension overlaying Smart Citations on journal sites.
Intended Audience: Researchers, librarians, research-integrity officers, publishers, universities, pharma regulatory and medical-affairs teams.
Use Cases: Checking whether a cited finding has actually been replicated or contested; screening a manuscript's reference list for retracted work; assessing the real influence of a paper beyond raw citation count; research-integrity review.
Best For: Verifying whether a claim has held up in the literature since publication.
Pricing Model: Subscription; heavy institutional licensing
Pricing Plans: Personal plan around $20/mo or roughly $144-180/yr billed annually. Student pricing reduced. Institutional and enterprise licences quoted per organisation (typically the main revenue model). A free limited view is available via the browser extension and some public pages.
Usage Limits: Free access shows limited Smart Citation detail; full citation statements and Reference Check require a subscription. Institutional access is the normal route for universities.
Free Plan: Limited free access - basic Smart Citation badges via the browser extension and some public reports.
Free Trial: Yes - a short free trial of the Personal plan is typically offered; institutional trials via sales.
Platforms: Web, browser extensions (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
Languages: English interface; corpus predominantly English
API: Yes - Scite API available on paid and institutional plans
Integrations: Zotero, EndNote, Mendeley, ORCID, publisher platforms, institutional discovery layers, browser extension overlays on PubMed/journals
Advantages: The supporting/contrasting distinction is genuinely unique and directly useful for research integrity; Reference Check catches retracted citations before publication; deep institutional integrations; strong library adoption.
Limitations: Coverage depends on full-text access agreements, so some citation statements are missing; classification accuracy is good but imperfect; individual pricing is high relative to Consensus; narrow use case outside academia.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Most valuable as a verification layer rather than a discovery tool. For a literature review, pair Scite (does this hold up?) with Elicit (what does the literature say?).
Evidence / Sources: scite.ai/pricing; help.scite.ai
Logo Source: Logo and press kit on site
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Editorial use acceptable; confirm commercial reuse with Research Solutions.

Overview: All-in-one academic research workspace: an AI copilot that explains papers line by line, a literature review table builder, a paraphraser, an AI detector and a manuscript formatter for 40,000+ journal templates.
Main Features: Copilot that explains any highlighted text, equation or figure in a PDF; literature review tables with custom columns; paper search across 280M+ papers; AI writer and paraphraser; AI content detector; journal template formatter; citation generator; Deep Review reports.
Intended Audience: Graduate students, early-career researchers, non-native English speakers reading English literature, thesis writers.
Use Cases: Understanding a difficult paper section by section; building a comparison table across 20 papers; formatting a manuscript to a target journal's template; paraphrasing and language polishing for non-native writers; generating a first-pass literature review.
Best For: Reading and understanding dense papers, especially for non-native English speakers.
Pricing Model: Freemium subscription
Pricing Plans: Free tier with limited monthly messages and uploads. Premium around $12-20/mo billed annually (higher billed monthly). Advanced/Pro tiers around $20-40/mo for higher limits and Deep Review. Team and institutional pricing on request. Verify - SciSpace repackages tiers frequently.
Usage Limits: Free tier caps Copilot messages, PDF uploads and literature-table rows per month. Deep Review and high-volume extraction are paid-tier features.
Free Plan: Yes - free tier with limited Copilot messages and uploads.
Free Trial: Short paid trials offered periodically; free tier is the main evaluation route.
Platforms: Web, Chrome extension, iOS and Android apps
Languages: Copilot explains in 75+ languages including Arabic and French - a genuine differentiator
API: Limited; contact for institutional access
Integrations: Zotero, Mendeley, citation export, Chrome extension over journal sites, Word export
Advantages: The explain-this-paragraph Copilot is excellent for hard material; multilingual explanation of English papers is a real advantage for non-native speakers; journal formatting saves hours; very broad feature set for the price.
Limitations: Breadth comes at the cost of depth - each feature is weaker than the best-in-class specialist; AI-detector accuracy is unreliable and should not be used for academic-integrity decisions; paraphrasing raises plagiarism-policy questions; tier structure changes often.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: Do not rely on the built-in AI detector for any consequential judgement - detectors in general have high false-positive rates on non-native English writing. Use SciSpace for comprehension, Elicit for extraction.
Evidence / Sources: typeset.io/pricing; SciSpace help centre
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Confirm reuse permission with SciSpace before commercial use.

Overview: Source-grounded research and note-taking tool. You upload your own documents, PDFs, Drive files, URLs, YouTube videos or pasted text, and every answer is generated strictly from those sources with inline citations back to the exact passage.
Main Features: Grounding strictly in uploaded sources (no open-web drift); inline citations to source passages; Audio Overview generating a two-host podcast discussion of your sources; Video Overview; Mind Map; Study Guide, Briefing Doc, FAQ and Timeline generation; Notebook sharing; Discover to find sources.
Intended Audience: Students, researchers, analysts, consultants, legal and compliance teams, anyone synthesising a defined document set.
Use Cases: Studying from lecture notes and textbooks; synthesising a set of client documents; producing a briefing from 20 reports; generating an audio summary of dense material for a commute; onboarding on a new codebase or policy set.
Best For: Answering questions from a closed, trusted set of your own documents.
Pricing Model: Free with paid limits raised through the Google AI subscription ladder
Pricing Plans: Free with generous limits (typically 100 notebooks, 50 sources each). NotebookLM Pro capabilities are bundled into Google AI Pro at $19.99/mo and Google AI Ultra at $99.99/$199.99, raising notebook and source limits roughly 5x and adding higher Audio Overview quotas. Also available through Google Workspace with admin controls.
Billing Period: Monthly or annual via Google AI plans
Usage Limits: Free tier caps notebooks, sources per notebook, daily chat queries and Audio Overview generations. Paid tiers multiply these roughly 5x. Individual source size limits apply (word/page count per document).
Free Plan: Yes - substantial free tier that covers most individual use.
Free Trial: Google AI Pro trials appear periodically; the free NotebookLM tier is the practical trial.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android
Languages: Supports 35+ languages for output; Audio Overviews available in a growing set including Arabic and French
API: Limited public API; Workspace admin APIs for enterprise deployment
Integrations: Google Drive, Docs, Slides, YouTube, PDF/URL/text upload, Google Workspace
Advantages: Grounding is strict - it will say the sources do not contain an answer rather than invent one, which is the single most valuable property for professional use; Audio Overview is a genuinely novel and useful output format; free tier is unusually generous; no training on your uploaded content.
Limitations: Cannot search the open web, by design, so it is useless for current-events research; source size and count limits bite on large corpora; Audio Overview quality varies and can be superficial; limited export and no deep workflow integration.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: The strict grounding makes it the safest option in this list for regulated or client-confidential material. Confirm your organisation's data-handling posture for Workspace vs consumer accounts before uploading sensitive documents.
Evidence / Sources: notebooklm.google.com; support.google.com/notebooklm; one.google.com/about/google-ai-plans
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Google Brand Permissions govern reuse; editorial screenshots generally permitted.

Overview: AI tutor and teaching assistant from the non-profit Khan Academy, built on GPT models and tuned to Socratic tutoring - it guides students to the answer rather than giving it, and gives teachers lesson planning and progress insight.
Main Features: Socratic tutoring that withholds direct answers; writing coach; debate practice partner; teacher tools for lesson planning, rubric and quiz generation; progress reports and student activity transcripts for teachers and parents; integration with Khan Academy's full curriculum; safety guardrails and moderation logging.
Intended Audience: K-12 students, teachers, school districts, parents and homeschoolers.
Use Cases: One-to-one maths and reading tutoring; essay coaching; generating differentiated lesson plans; creating quizzes aligned to standards; giving parents visibility into a child's learning.
Best For: Socratic K-12 tutoring with adult oversight built in.
Pricing Model: Free for US teachers (district/philanthropy funded); low-cost subscription for parents; district licensing
Pricing Plans: Free for US educators (funded by districts and philanthropy). Parents/learners around $4/mo or $44/yr. District and school licensing quoted per student, typically $35-45 per student per year. Availability and pricing vary substantially by country.
Billing Period: Monthly or annual for individuals; annual per-student for districts
Usage Limits: Usage limits are light for individuals. Availability is US-centric; many features and the free educator tier are not offered in all countries.
Free Plan: Free for verified US teachers. Khan Academy's core content remains free worldwide; Khanmigo itself is paid for parents.
Free Trial: Free trial periods offered for parent accounts; district pilots via sales.
Platforms: Web, iOS, Android; integrates with Khan Academy platform
Languages: English primary; Spanish and a growing set of languages; not strong in Arabic
API: No public API
Integrations: Khan Academy curriculum, Google Classroom, Clever, ClassLink, Canvas (district tiers)
Advantages: Non-profit mission and pricing - by far the cheapest credible AI tutor; the Socratic design genuinely resists doing the homework for the student; teacher and parent oversight is built into the product rather than bolted on; strong safety posture for minors.
Limitations: Tied to Khan Academy's curriculum and pedagogy; weaker outside maths and core subjects; limited non-English support; availability restricted outside the US; tutoring quality still varies on advanced topics.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: The oversight transcripts are the feature that matters most for school deployment - every student conversation is reviewable by a teacher or parent. Confirm availability in your country before planning around it.
Evidence / Sources: khanmigo.ai; khanacademy.org/khan-labs; Khan Academy district resources

Overview: A large library of 80+ purpose-built AI tools for teachers - lesson plans, rubrics, IEP goals, parent emails, differentiated texts - plus a separate safe student-facing environment (MagicStudent) with teacher-monitored rooms.
Main Features: 80+ task-specific generators (lesson plan, unit plan, rubric, exit ticket, IEP goal, behaviour intervention, parent email translated into any language); MagicStudent rooms with teacher monitoring and flagged-content alerts; Raina AI assistant; text leveller and translator; LMS integrations; district analytics dashboard.
Intended Audience: K-12 teachers, instructional coaches, special-education staff, school and district administrators.
Use Cases: Generating a differentiated lesson plan in minutes; writing IEP goals; drafting a sensitive parent email and translating it into the family's home language; levelling a reading passage for mixed abilities; building rubrics.
Best For: Cutting teacher administrative workload with task-specific generators.
Pricing Model: Freemium for individual teachers; per-teacher or per-student district licensing
Pricing Plans: Free plan for individual educators covering most tools with monthly generation limits. MagicSchool Plus around $99.96/yr (about $8.33/mo) per teacher for unlimited generations and premium tools. Enterprise/district licensing quoted per teacher or per student, typically with LMS/SIS integration, SSO and admin analytics included.
Billing Period: Annual for individual Plus and district licences
Usage Limits: Free tier caps monthly generations and limits access to some premium tools and MagicStudent room capacity.

Integrations: Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology, Clever, ClassLink, Google Drive, Microsoft Teams for Education

Pricing Plans: Free tier for individual teachers with limited Spaces and student seats. Paid teacher tier roughly $10-15/mo. Languages: Multilingual output; interface primarily English

Overview: Student study platform that turns uploaded course materials - lecture slides, PDFs, notes, recorded lectures - into flashcards, practice tests, summaries and an AI tutor called Spark.E that answers questions from those materials.
Main Features: Upload lectures/PDFs/slides and auto-generate flashcards, quizzes and notes; Spark.E AI tutor grounded in your materials; lecture recording and transcription; spaced-repetition flashcards; practice tests with explanations; study-time analytics; Classroom mode for instructors.

Overview: Neural machine translation service widely regarded as producing the most natural-sounding output, particularly between European languages. Now extended with DeepL Write (a monolingual style and grammar editor) and DeepL Voice for live meeting translation.
Main Features: Document translation preserving formatting (DOCX, PPTX, PDF, XLSX, HTML); glossaries enforcing terminology; formal/informal tone control; DeepL Write for rephrasing and style; DeepL Voice for real-time meeting and conversation translation; Clarify for ambiguous-source questions; desktop apps with a global hotkey; browser extensions.
Intended Audience: Professional translators, legal and technical writers, international businesses, localisation teams, and anyone drafting in a second language.
Use Cases: Translating contracts and technical documentation while keeping layout; enforcing approved terminology across a company; polishing English written by a non-native speaker; live translation in Teams meetings; translating a website.
Best For: High-quality document translation between well-supported European languages with terminology control.
Pricing Model: Freemium; per-seat subscription; separate character-metered API
Pricing Plans: Free with strict limits. Starter around $8.74/user/mo billed annually. Advanced around $28.99/user/mo annually. Ultimate around $57.49/user/mo annually. DeepL API Free allows 500,000 characters/month at no cost; DeepL API Pro is roughly $5.49/mo plus about $25 per million characters. Prices vary by region and currency (EUR pricing differs from USD).
Currency: USD, EUR, GBP and others by region
Usage Limits: Free web tier caps text at ~1,500-5,000 characters per translation and 3 document translations per month with size limits and no editing of the output file. Paid tiers raise or remove document counts by tier. API Free is hard-capped at 500,000 characters/month.
Free Plan: Yes - free web and app translation with character and document limits, plus a free API tier of 500,000 characters/month.
Free Trial: Yes - 30-day free trial typically offered on Pro plans.
Platforms: Web, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Chrome/Edge/Firefox extensions, Word and Outlook add-ins
Languages: 30+ languages including Arabic (added later than others), French, English, and all major European languages; quality is notably highest between European pairs
API: Yes - DeepL API with free and Pro tiers, character-metered; well-documented REST API with official SDKs
Integrations: Microsoft Word, Outlook, Teams, Google Workspace, Chrome, Trados, memoQ, Zendesk, Salesforce, Confluence, Jira, Slack
Advantages: Consistently rated the most natural translation output in its strongest language pairs; glossaries give genuine terminology control; document translation preserves complex formatting well; strong GDPR posture with EU data processing and no training on Pro data; clean, well-documented API.
Limitations: Language coverage is far narrower than Google Translate; Arabic and non-European languages are noticeably weaker than French/German/Spanish; free tier limits are restrictive; per-seat pricing adds up for large teams; DeepL Voice availability is limited by platform and language.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: For Arabic work, test against Google Translate and Microsoft Translator before standardising - DeepL's advantage is much smaller outside European pairs. The API Free tier at 500K characters/month is genuinely useful for prototyping.
Evidence / Sources: deepl.com/pro; deepl.com/pro-api; DeepL privacy and security documentation
Screenshot / Reuse Information: Press kit publicly available; editorial reuse permitted with attribution.

Use Cases: Translating a product documentation set into 20 languages with human post-editing; managing and paying a freelance linguist pool; localising video with dubbing and subtitles; continuous website and app localisation.

Billing Period: Monthly or annual; enterprise annual with volume commitment
Usage Limits: Word-volume allowances per plan with overage pricing; seat counts per tier; some connectors and AI features restricted to higher tiers.

Languages: 280+ languages including Arabic and French; automatic MT engine selection per pair
API: Yes - full REST API plus CLI for CI/CD localisation pipelines

Limitations: Complex product with a real learning curve; pricing is opaque and negotiated, making budgeting hard; marketplace linguist quality varies and needs vetting; overkill for small or occasional translation needs; word-overage charges can surprise.

Limitations: Expensive - entry pricing is well above Smartcat or Crowdin for small teams; priced for software strings, not documents; steep setup investment before value appears; AI word metering on top of seat cost makes total cost hard to predict; no meaningful free tier.

Overview: AI-plus-human translation layer purpose-built for multilingual customer support. It sits inside the helpdesk so agents write in their own language and customers receive fluent translated replies, with human editors in the loop where quality thresholds demand it.
Main Features: Widn.AI translation models; real-time translation inside Zendesk/Salesforce/Intercom tickets and chat; human-in-the-loop editing triggered by quality scoring; MT Quality Estimation (COMET-based) that predicts translation quality without a reference; customer-specific glossaries and tone; Unbabel LangOps analytics; multilingual chat and email.

Overview: Source-available workflow automation platform that can be self-hosted for free. Combines a visual node editor with the ability to drop into JavaScript or Python, and has become the default choice for building AI agent workflows with full data control.
Main Features: Self-hostable (Docker, Kubernetes, npm) with no execution limits on the community edition; visual node editor plus custom code nodes; native LangChain integration for AI agent workflows; vector store nodes (Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase, PGVector); AI Agent node with tool calling; 1,000+ integrations plus universal HTTP node; sub-workflows; queue mode for scale; MCP client and server nodes.
Intended Audience: Developers, technical operations teams, AI engineers, and organisations with data-residency requirements.
Use Cases: Building RAG pipelines and AI agents with full control over data; automating internal processes on-premises for compliance; orchestrating LLM calls across providers with fallback logic; replacing an expensive Zapier bill with self-hosted infrastructure.

Pricing Model: Free self-hosted (fair-code licence); paid cloud tiers by execution volume; enterprise self-hosted licence
Pricing Plans: Community Edition free and self-hosted with unlimited workflows and executions (Sustainable Use Licence - free for internal business use, restrictions on reselling as a service). n8n Cloud Starter from roughly EUR 20-24/mo (2,500 executions, 5 active workflows). Free Trial: Yes - free trial of n8n Cloud; self-hosting is free indefinitely.
Platforms: Self-hosted (Docker, Kubernetes, npm, Railway, Render); n8n Cloud; desktop app
Languages: Interface in English and several community translations

Integrations: 1,000+ nodes including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Hugging Face, Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase, Postgres, MySQL, Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, plus a universal HTTP node
Advantages: Per-execution rather than per-step billing makes it dramatically cheaper than Zapier at any real volume; self-hosting eliminates both cost and data-residency concerns; native LangChain and vector-store nodes make it the strongest platform here for building real AI agents; code nodes remove the no-code ceiling.
Limitations: Genuinely requires technical skill - self-hosting means you own updates, backups, scaling and security; the licence is fair-code, not true open source, and restricts some commercial uses; UI is less polished than Make; fewer prebuilt connectors than Zapier; community support rather than SLA unless you buy enterprise.
Evaluation / Testing Notes: The per-execution billing model is the headline economic advantage - a workflow with 50 nodes costs the same as one with 2. For any team with a developer and a compliance requirement, self-hosted n8n is usually the correct answer in this category.

Overview: Generates advertising creatives - banners, social ads, video ads and text - trained on performance data so it scores each generated asset for likely conversion rate before you spend money on it.

Use Cases: Generating 50 ad variants for a campaign test in minutes; predicting which creative will convert before spending budget; producing platform-correct sizes without a designer; generating product lifestyle imagery without a photoshoot; analysing competitor creative strategy.

Pricing Model: Credit-based subscription tiers by credits and brands
Pricing Plans: Starter tiers from around $39-49/mo (limited credits, 1 brand). Professional tiers around $99-149/mo with more credits and brands. Ultimate/Scale tiers around $249-599/mo for agencies with many brands and high credit volumes. Enterprise custom. Annual billing discounted. Languages: Ad text generation in 30+ languages including Arabic and French
API: Yes - API available on higher tiers
Integrations: Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, LinkedIn Ads, Google Analytics, Shopify, WooCommerce, Zapier, Canva, Dropbox
